name: /mock-exam-paper
description: Builds a timed mock exam with marks, sections and a marking guide from your syllabus topics.
author: Promptzyra
install:
1. Create the folder .claude/commands in your project (or ~/.claude/commands for all projects).
2. Save the file below as mock-exam-paper.md; the filename becomes the command name.
3. In Claude Code, type /mock-exam-paper followed by your input.
4. Edit the instructions to match your course or style.

files.content:
---
description: Builds a timed mock exam with marks, sections and a marking guide from your syllabus topics.
argument-hint: [subject] [duration in minutes] [topics...]
---

Create a mock exam for $ARGUMENTS.

1. Split into sections (short answer, structured, extended) with marks per question.
2. Make total marks match the stated duration at about one mark per minute.
3. Cover each listed topic at least once.
4. After the paper, add a marking guide with expected points and common errors.

Do not reveal the marking guide until the paper is finished.

name: /past-paper-analyzer
description: Finds recurring topics, question styles and mark weightings across pasted past papers.
author: Promptzyra
install:
1. Create the folder .claude/commands in your project (or ~/.claude/commands for all projects).
2. Save the file below as past-paper-analyzer.md; the filename becomes the command name.
3. In Claude Code, type /past-paper-analyzer followed by your input.
4. Edit the instructions to match your course or style.

files.content:
---
description: Finds recurring topics, question styles and mark weightings across pasted past papers.
argument-hint: [paste past paper questions]
---

Analyze the past paper questions in $ARGUMENTS.

1. Group questions by topic and count how often each appears.
2. Note command words used (explain, evaluate, compare) and what each expects.
3. Rank topics by likely weight in the next exam, saying this is an estimate.
4. Suggest a three-point revision priority list.

Base every claim only on the pasted questions.

description: Condenses a topic into a one-page last-minute revision sheet of must-know facts.

1. Create the folder .claude/commands in your project (or ~/.claude/commands for all projects).
2. Save the file below as star-answer-coach.md; the filename becomes the command name.
3. In Claude Code, type /star-answer-coach followed by your input.
4. Edit the instructions to match your course or style.

files.content:
---
description: Coaches behavioural interview answers using the STAR structure and gives feedback.
argument-hint: [question] [your draft answer]
---

Coach the answer in $ARGUMENTS using STAR.

1. Check whether Situation, Task, Action and Result are all present.
2. Mark vague parts and ask for specifics or measurable results.
3. Rewrite the answer in about 150 words, using only facts the user supplied.
4. Give one tip on delivery or length.

Do not invent achievements.

description: Runs a one-question-at-a-time mock interview and scores each answer.

install:

4. Edit the instructions to match your course or style.

files.content:
---
description: Runs a one-question-at-a-time mock interview and scores each answer.
argument-hint: [role] [company type]
---

Run a mock interview for $ARGUMENTS.

1. Ask one question at a time and wait for the answer.
2. Mix an opener, two role-specific, one behavioural and one curveball.
3. After each answer, give a score from 1-5 and one improvement.
4. At the end, summarize strengths and top three fixes.

Stay in character as a friendly but realistic interviewer.

files.content:
---
description: Gives coding interview style problems with hints on demand and a complexity review.
argument-hint: [language] [difficulty]
---

Start a technical interview drill for $ARGUMENTS.

1. Present one problem with input and output examples.
2. Do not give the solution; offer hints one level at a time when asked.
3. When the user submits code, review correctness, edge cases and time and space complexity.
4. Suggest a follow-up variation.

Stay quiet about the optimal approach until the user attempts it.

description: Prepares talking points, evidence and next steps for a parent-teacher conference.

---

Prepare for a parent-teacher conference about $ARGUMENTS.

1. Start with two genuine strengths of the student.
2. State one or two concerns using observable facts, not labels.
3. Suggest three questions to ask the parent.
4. Propose a shared action plan with dates.

Keep a respectful, solution-focused tone and avoid including sensitive details not provided.
